free_tier.stated: 10 MB per .crate file. No limit on versions per crate ('There is no limit to the number of versions which can be published'), no documented cap on total crates or total bytes per account.
free_tier.notes: the headline offer as the seed recorded it; the binding constraint is in limits[]

per_object_cap.stated: no per-object cap was extracted from the seed's quota and limits prose; absence here is a gap in this conversion, not a vendor claim that no cap exists
per_object_cap.notes: extraction found no per-object clause; some of these providers meter on object count rather than bytes, and some state no cap

retention.stated: | Effectively permanent — 'the code cannot be deleted', 'publish is generally permanent'

egress.terms: Free and unmetered, Cloudflare-fronted, CORS-open. Probe: static.crates.io .crate GET -> 200, Server: cloudflare, Cache-Control: 'public,max-age=31536000,immutable', Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *, Accept-Ranges: bytes.

tooling: PUT /api/v1/crates/new (binary metadata+body protocol), GET https://static.crates.io/crates/<name>/<name>-<ver>.crate. Clients: cargo publish, cargo-upload style wrappers. No rclone backend.
chaining: UNBOUNDED on crates x versions but throttled hard: 5 new crates burst then 1 per 10 minutes; 30 versions burst then 1 per minute. At 10 MB/crate, 10 TiB needs ~1,048,576 crates — at 1 new crate per 10 min that is ~20 years, so crates.io is *capacity*-unlimited and *throughput*-useless for bulk. Use it as a low-priority shard, not the primary.
limits_note: 10 MB per .crate. Publish rate: burst 5 new crates, then 1 per 10 min; burst 30 new versions, then 1 per minute (documented, leaky-bucket). No delete after 72h unless <1000 downloads/month-per-month AND no dependents AND single owner. Version numbers can never be reused or overwritten.

identity_cost.detail: no identity_cost field and no identity statement in the source record; defaulted to email and flagged, not evidence

reliability_note: Effectively permanent — 'the code cannot be deleted', 'publish is generally permanent'. Excellent durability, terrible write throughput: ~144 crates/day sustained, i.e. ~1.4 GB/day at 10 MB. Never disappears, but you cannot fill it fast.
